Algebra 1 | Quarter 2 | Unit 3: Linear Relationships

Climb, Descent, Flat or Drop

Which way is the trail going?

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 8–9
Topic
Positive and Negative Slope
Standards
8.EE.B.6, 8.F.B.4, HSF-LE.A.1

Students classify slopes as positive, negative, zero or undefined, connect each to the direction of a line and a section of trail, and explain why a vertical line has no slope.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Classify a slope as positive, negative, zero or undefined from a graph, two points or a description.
  • Connect the sign of the slope to the direction of a line read left to right.
  • Explain why a horizontal line has slope 0 and a vertical line has an undefined slope.
  • Compare the steepness of two lines using |m|.

3Essential question

What does the sign of a slope tell a rider about the trail ahead?

5MTB connection

A trail profile is made of four kinds of section: climbs (positive slope), descents (negative slope), flats (zero slope) and drops (in the extreme, vertical: undefined slope). Riders shift gears and position for each one.

A rider dropping off a ledge isn’t on a slope at all for that moment: the trail’s horizontal run is zero, which is exactly what “undefined” means.

The mathOn the trail
m > 0A climb
m < 0A descent
m = 0A flat section
Undefined mA vertical drop
Larger |m|Steeper, climbing or descending
